title: Relative endomorphism planar operad of a coherent functor
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, cores and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], its cartesian operadic envelope of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], and ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ as defined in [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. All categories and functor categories fit in fixed containing universes. Let $f:A\to B$ be any coherent functor. For each $r\geq0$, choose a replete full subcategory $C_r\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(B^r,B)$, where replete means closed under equivalence. Assume $\mathrm{id}_B\in C_1$ and that $v\in C_k$ and $w_i\in C_{r_i}$ imply $v(w_1,\ldots,w_k)\in C_{r_1+\cdots+r_k}$, using consecutive disjoint input lists, including empty lists.

Form the one-color endomorphism planar operad $E_A$ by restricting the cartesian envelope of $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ to tuples of the object $A$ and to ordered blocks. Similarly form the endomorphism planar operad of the object $f$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)$ with its pointwise cartesian product. Retain precisely those operations whose target-endpoint functor belongs to the corresponding $C_r$; call the resulting operation suboperad $E_C(f)$. The analogous restriction of the endomorphism planar operad of $B$ is denoted $E_C(B)$. These constructions give ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads and endpoint morphisms
$$E_A\xleftarrow{p}E_C(f)\xrightarrow{q}E_C(B).$$
Their fixed-color $r$-ary operation spaces are naturally
$$E_A(r)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,A)^\simeq,\qquad E_C(B)(r)=C_r^\simeq,$$
$$E_C(f)(r)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,A)^\simeq\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,B)^\simeq}C_r^\simeq,$$
where the maps to the middle space are $u\mapsto fu$ and $v\mapsto vf^r$. Thus an operation is $(u,v,\eta)$ with $\eta:vf^r\simeq fu$; $p$ and $q$ retain $u$ and $v$. Substitution uses disjoint ordered blocks and pastes these natural equivalences. The unary identity is $(\mathrm{id}_A,\mathrm{id}_B,\mathrm{id}_f)$, and arity zero is included. For a base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, let $a=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[m]\to[n]$ and $s_j=a(j)-a(j-1)$. Between the tuple objects of either of these one-color operads, the mapping space over $\alpha$ is the product of its operation spaces of arities $s_j$, $1\leq j\leq m$, with empty product a point. The total mapping space is the disjoint union of these spaces over base arrows. The endpoint maps respect these formulas and all substitution simplices.

Let $J$ be the identity-only one-color planar operad, with just the unary identity as single-output operation, and let $\mathsf{Ass}_{\mathrm{pl}}=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the planar associative operad with its unique operation in each arity, including zero. Derived operadic mapping spaces under $J$ fix the color together with its identification; they do not quotient the underlying object by its automorphisms. The space $\operatorname{Map}_{J/}(\mathsf{Ass}_{\mathrm{pl}},E_A)$ is the space of unital planar operation systems on the fixed category $A$ in the sense of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence], with unary identity identified with $\mathrm{id}_A$. The corresponding mapping space with target $E_C(f)$ is the space of such systems on $A$ and $B$, with every $B$-operation in $C_r$, together with coherent natural equivalences along the fixed functor $f$ making it a morphism of systems. The endpoint maps forget to the two systems. Evaluation at the arity-$r$ corolla is exactly evaluation to the operation spaces just displayed. These identifications include all tree contraction, grafting, identity and nullary coherences, commute with additional simplicial parameters, and identify homotopy fibers with spaces of these data equipped with their specified identifications.

source.place: Agent-formulated arrow-endomorphism construction using HA Remark 2.1.3.4 (pointwise monoidal functor categories), section 2.4.1 (cartesian structures), and Definitions 4.1.3.2, 4.1.3.9, 4.1.3.16 (planar operads and associative sections). These places were read online; the relative operation-suboperad formula and fixed-color mapping-space interpretation are the explicit auxiliary assertion, not a verbatim theorem of HA.
